confidence_note: Concept; the three-phase weekly review (Get Clear, Get Current, Get Creative) is confirmed only in secondary summaries and Allen's company material, not the book text; steps are kept generic. Old text's one-hour ritual, 'mental integration' and 'GTD without review is just a list' were dropped.
facts: Allen asks for a regular, preferably weekly, review of all lists.
Allen's workflow has five stages: collect, process, organize, review, do; the weekly review is the 'review' stage that keeps the other four current.
Three phases: Get Clear, Get Current, Get Creative.
Get Clear: collect loose papers and materials, empty the inbox, empty your head.
Get Current: review next-action lists, calendar past and upcoming, waiting-for list and project lists.
Get Creative: look over someday/maybe items.
tension: A system you built works for a while, then the world moves and you stop trusting it.
opening_idea: Open on the three words: clear, current, creative, and the list that is out of date.

lessons.idea: A list you trust has to be refreshed on a schedule.
lessons.example: A shared grocery list that nobody updates gets ignored and everyone buys by memory.

reflect_final: Which list or calendar of yours is furthest out of date, and when this week will you sit down to bring it current?

use_cases.move: Spend a short slot looking at each list and removing what is done, as in Allen's Get Current.

use_cases.situation: A team board has drifted from reality.
use_cases.move: Propose a weekly check of the next-action and waiting-for items.

use_cases.situation: A friend says they abandoned their system.
use_cases.move: Ask what they stopped looking at; suggest one weekly look.

pocket_idea: A list you trust needs a weekly check: clear the inbox, bring the lists current, then look at someday.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Allen's weekly review keeps a list trustworthy.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: David Allen's Weekly Review has three steps: get clear, get current, get creative. Empty the inbox, check each list against what is really going on, then look at what you might do someday.
